audit.whatIsWrong: Row 0 read 'Skill' and rows 5 and 6 read 'Volibear' / 'Skill' in both layers; the packet chart gives Volibear / Yasuo / Yasuo. The content whys already said 'You crush level 1-2', 'First item swings to Yasuo' and 'Late game Yasuo out-scales', so three rows printed a token against their own sentence.
audit.why: Level 1 is a genuine Volibear win — his stat block plus Thundering Smash against a Yasuo whose trading pattern needs minions to Sweeping Blade between. From first item his crit spike plus the Way of the Wanderer moving shield out-damages a bruiser Volibear, and at two items he is a crit hypercarry with lifesteal and Wind Wall. A 54.72% win rate over 2235 games is consistent with owning levels 1-5 and losing the item stages.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 5 and 6 set to the packet sides in both layers as one atomic group, ratings moved to 7/10, 4/10 and 3/10, and the three full-layer whys rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[5].why and phases[6].why both handed the item stages to Volibear ('Force Yasuo to fight or lose the wave', 'a drain-tank Yasuo can't burst'), inverting the two stages Yasuo takes.
audit.why: Way of the Wanderer gives him a shield that builds while he moves and triggers on the first champion damage he takes, which blunts exactly the poke Sundered Sky wants to trade with, and his first crit item is a step change in damage. Late, Last Breath drops to 30s at rank 3, so 'wait out his ult' stops being a plan.
audit.corrected: phases[5].why now names the crit item plus the passive shield and redirects to the map; phases[6].why names the hypercarry scaling and reframes Stormbringer as a teamfight lockdown tool.

audit.whatIsWrong: Volibear's Q is called a slow in four fields — whys[0], spikes[0].text, content.early and content.mid all say 'Q slow'. spikes[0].text also calls Frenzied Maul a 'shred'.
audit.why: Thundering Smash (Q, 12/11.5/11/10.5/10s, 300 range) stuns and damages the first enemy he attacks; it is a stun and an auto-attack reset, not a slow. The slow in Volibear's kit is Sky Splitter (E, 16s) and Stormbringer (R, 160/135/110s). Against Yasuo the distinction is the entire lane: a slow does not stop Sweeping Blade, a stun does, and that is what makes his dash-out punishable.
audit.corrected: All four fields now say Q stun / Thundering Smash, and Frenzied Maul is described by what it does — the second bite on a marked target.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0].text asserts 'windwall only eats E' and wants.foe[1] says he should 'save windwall for your E Sky Splitter' — i.e. that Wind Wall blocks Sky Splitter. I could not verify this and did not change or endorse it.
audit.why: The kit file's derived flags mark Sky Splitter as a projectile, but Riot's own description says Volibear 'summons a lightning bolt at a location' — a ground-targeted effect, not a fired projectile. Per the run's rule, where a derived flag contradicts Riot's description the description wins, so the projectile flag here is suspect and the Wind Wall claim is unproven either way. Wind Wall eligibility is exactly the class of fact the kits deliberately do not answer.

packet.suspectNames flagged "W's Frenzied Maul" in spikes[0].text as a probable wrong name. FALSE POSITIVE — Frenzied Maul is Volibear's real W; the flag fired on the "W's" prefix. The surrounding phrase was reworded anyway because 'shred' misdescribes what the ability does, not because the name was wrong.

I deliberately left the 'Wind Wall blocks Sky Splitter' claim in spikes[0].text and wants.foe[1] untouched: the kit's projectile flag says yes but Riot's own text calls Sky Splitter a lightning bolt summoned at a location, and Wind Wall eligibility is not answerable from the kits.
